why: Senj baptisms, page 122, entry 96 gives the birth as 9 October and the baptism as 17 October. The tree's 19 is a transcription slip against the register it cites.

The 1920 marriage register, written in his lifetime from his baptismal certificate, gives 1892 1/III. The stone was cut after 1966 from memory. The archive follows the register and records the stone as wrong.

tree: Wife of Michael Žubrinić; mother of Nicolaus (b. 24 January 1834)
record: Born 8 September 1835 — twenty months after her supposed son

The transcription is right and the attachment is wrong. Nicolaus's own 1834 entry names his mother as an Orešković, but an earlier one, still unidentified. Six further ancestors hang below this join.

tree: Asserted, with no document — this archive called it Disputed
record: Documented: Senj marriages, 8 December 1920, page 366 entry 41
why: The marriage entry names the groom's parents as Juraj Blažević and Tereza r. Žubrinić, and annotates them mrt. — deceased — which puts Juraj's death before December 1920. He remains undated and unplaced, and nothing yet links him to Toma above.

The Vrbnik baptisms for 1806, house 244, read: Die 14. Martii Ao 1806 baptizavi ego Michaël Kombol C.L. infantem lege natum patre Joanne, Matre Marthæ Antich Papa, nomine Josephum. The tree's date is exact. The entry also names his father Joannes (ahnentafel 48) and his mother Martha, and gives the godparents as the village judge Mathias Jellichich and his wife Margarita.

record: Josephus — and the priest wrote the accusative himself
why: The register reads nomine Josephum. That is the priest's own Latin, not a modern transcriber's slip: Michaël Kombol writes nomine followed by the accusative in every entry on the page — Mariam, Joannem, Matthæam, Magdalenam, Nicolaum. The tree copied the register faithfully and inherited its grammar.

The Karlobag register for August 1789 reads Mariam natam pridie ex Michaele et Lucia Gergacs. The register's spelling is Gergacs; Gerkacs is the secondary form and the tree carries it first. The entry also gives her mother as Lucia — written over a struck-out name — and her father as Michael.

record: August 1789, born the day before baptism — consistent
why: The entry says natam pridie, born the previous day, and sits in the August 1789 sequence after the entry of 9 August. That is consistent with 11 August but the scan does not itself carry a day number; the exact day comes from the index, not the page.

record: April 1777, Karlobag, born the day before — consistent
why: The Karlobag register reads: baptizavi Infantem heri natum ex Georgio et Maria Uroda Conjugibus hujus Loci, cui impositum est Nomen Joannis Georgij. It confirms the year, the place and both parents, and shows he was born the day before the baptism — but the page carries no day number, so 22 April comes from the index rather than the register. The godparents are Pro-Colonel Joannes Hallinich de Zirfeld and the wife of Captain Daniel de Hofenegg: Military Frontier officers standing for a Karlobag child.

what: She is not this child's mother

Her own 1835 baptism names the same parents the tree gives her and places her at Dubrava N° 29, so she is a real person married here to the wrong man. The join is kept and marked rather than severed, because a wrong join is itself a finding and the only pointer to where the right Maria Orešković should be looked for.

why: The Otočac baptism of his son Josephus, 16 March 1845, gives the mother as Maria Žubrinić nata Marković; the 1834 baptism of Nicolaus gives Maria nata Orešković. Either the first wife died and he remarried a second Maria, or there are two men of this name — there are 68 Žubrinić records at Otočac. Nothing read so far chooses between them.

Senj marriages p.348 no.5, her own entry of 1 April 1918, gives 1884 12/5. The register is written from her baptismal certificate; the tree's 17 is five days out. The same entry gives her occupation as nadglednica u tvornici duhana — supervisor in the tobacco factory, not a floor worker — and her parents as Pavao Blažević and Marija r. Tomljanović, poljodjelci iz župe Krmpote.

what: Birth date, and her parents' house

The same entry gives her parents as ††Toma i Tereza Blažević, poljodjelci iz sela Smokvica kbr. 114 — both dead, and the house written out rather than inferred from a baptismal margin. tree: Michael “Mate” Žubrinić and Maria Catharina Orešković — the same couple as Nicolaus, b. 1834
record: Mate Žubrinić and Marija r. Orešković, both dead by 1910 — but a different couple
why: His marriage at Senj on 3 July 1910, where he is kontrolor gradske daće, names his parents as ††Mate Žubrinić i Marija rodj. Orešković, poljodjelci. So both he and Nicolaus (1834) have parents of these names — forty-six years apart. There are two couples of the same two names a generation apart, and the tree has merged them. By date, Maria Catharina (b. 1835) belongs to this later couple, not to the 1834 one.
Senj marriages p.355 no.18, her marriage to Viktor Matijević on 12 May 1919. She is entered radnica u tvornici duhana, of Krmpote, daughter of Pavao Blažević and Marija r. Tomljanović.

Senj marriages p.326 no.23, her marriage to Josip Nagoda on 5 October 1913. Entered radnica u tvornici duhana u Senju, iz župe sv. Jakov Krmpote; her parents Pavao Blažević and Marija r. Tomljanović, poljodjelci of the same parish.

tree: 26 July 1907, Senj — no cause, no burial detail
record: 26 July 1907, Senj — tuberculosis, aged 69, buried sv. Vid on 28 July
why: Senj deaths p.225 no.60: Blažević Toma, nadničar, udovac iza pok. Tereze, born sv. Jakov Krmpote, living Senj, 69 god., Tuberculosis, providjen, buried sv. Vid 28 srpnja. Sixty-nine in July 1907 matches his recorded birth of 27 January 1838. He died in the town as a day-labourer, not on the land at Smokvica.

Before 1850 is impossible: the same tree marries her to Toma on 21 November 1858 and gives her children in 1860, 1880, 1882 and 1884. Her husband's death entry of 26 July 1907 calls him udovac iza pok. Tereze — widower of the late Tereza — which is the only real bound anyone has. She was alive in 1884 and dead by July 1907.

Cammeralis nautae Vincentii Pilipich et Matthiae Uroda conjugum hujus Civitatis. The register names both parents and gives her father as nauta cameralis — a sailor of the Imperial Chamber, the Habsburg treasury's maritime service. The tree renders this as 'finansijski nadmornar. profesional financial arigilia nanta', which is a mangling of the same phrase.

record: Senj — the stone reads BLAŽEVIĆ TEREZA ✻1867 †1931
why: A photograph of the grave at Senj confirms both years the tree carries and supplies the burial place it leaves blank. The plot was restored by the Kosina family in 1991 — her daughter Anka's married family — and carries a wooden cross for vlč. Antun Kosina, 1921–2003.

tree: Born 12 January 1779 — the tree's own note adds “(Maybe)”
record: A real Karlobag baptism of that date, but of a different man
why: The Karlobag register of 12 January 1779 does record a Caetanus Antonius Bacchi, son of Angelo and Catharina, with a Captain as godfather and the wife of Dominus Georgius Uroda as godmother. But ahn 214's daughter Oliva Andreana died in 1795 and her daughter Oliva Maria Smojver was born 11 March 1781 — two years after this baptism. Two years cannot hold two generations. The right Caetano Bacchi belongs around 1730–1745, and this entry belongs to someone else of the name.

what: Attached on a baptism that is not his son's
record: Named only in the 1779 entry, which cannot be ahn 214's
why: Angelo and Catharina are in this pedigree solely because the 1779 Karlobag baptism names them as the child's parents. If that baptism belongs to a different Caetano Bacchi, they are that man's parents and not this line's. Nothing else anchors them — Catharina is one of the seven women here with no surname at all.

Ego Joës Antonius Ivankovich Parochus Loci baptizavi Infantem de 11ma hujus natam ex Vincentio, et Oliva Smoyver, vulgo Vukich, Conjugibus hujus Civitatis, cui impositum est nomen Oliva Maria. The alias Smojver vulgo Vukić is the register's own, and Karlobag is entered as a civitas — a city, not a village.

Josephum filium pridie natum a Domino Jacobo et Catharina Pilepich conjugibus hujus loci — pridie, the day before, so born 10 March. The family carries the honorific Dominus. Godparents Dominus Franciscus de Justiniani, a Venetian patrician name, and Domina Ursula, widow of Dominus Joannes Krixich.

tree: Born 12 May 1859, baptised 15 May 1859, Krivi Put 136
record: Confirmed exactly — and the household is entered Confiniarii
why: Krivi Put baptisms 1859, entry 51 (HDA 407, p.110): natus 12 Maji, baptisatus 15 Maji, Antonia Perpić, legit., Joannis et Luciæ Perpić filia, Confiniarii, Krivi Put N° 136. Godparents Lucas Tomljanović and Anna Tomljanović, daughter of Andreas. The word Confiniarii makes this a Military Frontier household — so Hedviga descends from Frontier families on the Prpić side as well as the Žubrinić.

tree: Married Antonija Prpić; trhonoša, bremenar, gostioničar
record: Married 3 May 1885 at Senj, aged 27, entered bremenar
why: Senj marriages p.192 no.5. He is 27 and she 26, matching births of 1857 and 1859. The entry names all four parents: Juraj Papa/Papić, težak, and Matea r. Pilipić; Ivan Perpić, seljak, and Luca. Witnesses Franjo and Toma Perpić, seljaci; Mirko Babić, kapelan.

what: Still no surname, after two documents
record: Two registers name her and neither gives one
why: Her daughter's 1859 baptism enters the parents as Joannis et Luciæ Perpić — the wife under her husband's name. Her daughter's 1885 marriage does give a maiden name, ending in -pić, but that scan is a 960-pixel thumbnail and the word cannot be read. A higher-resolution copy of that one entry would very likely give her a surname.

what: A child born after his death
why: Six years separate his death from his recorded child's birth. Either the death date, the birth date or the parentage is wrong; nothing here chooses between them. Left standing and marked rather than severed. Note that Vladimira Baricević — a different woman — is the mother of ten Boras children born before her own birth, so this branch has more than one bad join.

what: A child born 74 years after his death
why: Seventy-four years. This is not a loose date but a join across three or four generations — a Georgius Prpić of 1962 attached to a man who died in 1888. The intervening people are missing rather than wrong.

what: A child born after his death

what: A child born after his death
why: Two years. 1845 is the same year Elias Žubrinić and Ana Untersinger both died, which open question 4b suspects was an epidemic or famine year in Lika. If several Žubrinić deaths were entered as 1845 from memory rather than from a register, this may be one of them.

Six months backwards. The likeliest reading is that the two dates belong to two different children of the same name — a dead infant and the sibling named after her — which the name-reuse analysis found repeatedly in these families. That is a guess, and it is recorded as one.

tree: Born 21 June 1812; Lucas Ugrin Adamich born 1822
why: Ten years old. Either the child belongs to a different Magdalena or one of the two dates is wrong. Her husband Wolfgangus Adamich is recorded born 1813, which would make him nine, so the problem is with the child rather than with her.

what: A father in the same year as his son
record: An artefact of the hedge, not a contradiction
why: “BEF 1769” is somebody's estimate, made by working backwards from the son's birth. It is not a date anyone read. Flagged by the consistency check because the check cannot tell an estimate from a record, and kept here to say so rather than to dispute it.

tree: Smokvica, Krmpote, Općina Smokvica, Dubrovačko-neretvanska županija
record: Smokvica Krmpotska, Općina Novi Vinodolski, Primorje-Gorski Kotar
why: Općina Smokvica in Dubrovnik-Neretva county is Smokvica on the island of Korčula, 400 km south. The village meant is Smokvica Krmpotska, inland from Novi Vinodolski, and the tree names it in the same string — Krmpote. This is a geocoder matching the wrong Smokvica, not anybody's claim, which is why it is corrected outright rather than merely noted. It matters: Smokvica kbr. 114 and the parish of sv. Jakov Krmpote are the whole of question 1b.

Senj has never been in Split-Dalmatia. It is the seat of its own historic county and sits in Lika-Senj, 200 km north of Split. Another geocoder mismatch. He is the emigrant who reached Port Pirie, so this is the birthplace anyone tracing the Australian branch backwards will search on.

record: Died 3 June 1903 aged 1 year 8 months — scarlatina with diphtheria
why: Senj deaths p.162 no.52: Papić Stanko (Milan), sin, of nadničar Josip and Tonka Papić, Senj, 1 8/12 god, Scarlatina c. m. Diphtheritis, buried sv. Vid on 4 June. An age of one year eight months puts his birth about October 1901 rather than 1902. He died in a scarlet-fever outbreak that killed four people in Senj in eight days — including a second Papić child, from another household, the day before him.

tree: Mother Katarina “Kate” Matijavic; no father recorded
why: Senj deaths p.162 no.51: Papić Tereza, kći of nadničara Franje i Kate Papić, 4 7/12 god, Scarlatina, died 2 June 1903 and buried sv. Vid the next day. The register names the father the tree leaves blank. She died one day before Stanko Papić of the same disease, from a different Papić household.

record: Confirmed — and the civil entry is cited in her baptism margin

record: Born 23 October, baptised 25 October 1888, at Smokvica kbr. 114 — and died 30 June 1954 at Senj
why: Sv. Jakov Krmpote baptisms, HDA 111 p.104 no.60: Pave Blažević i Marija rodjena Tomljanović, seljaci, Smokvica kbr. 114. Godparents Ivo Blažević sin Matin and Anica Tomljanović. tree: No occupation recorded — her whole event list is born, immigrated, died

why: Remembered in the family and written down in September 2026. Nothing corroborates it, and nothing contradicts it — the tree simply says nothing about her working life at all. The venue is real and datable: the Therapia opened at Crikvenica in 1895 as the Nadvojvoda Josip, was renamed in 1899 when a hydropathic institute was put inside it, and with the Miramare of 1906 is the building that made Crikvenica a health resort. It still stands, renamed Kvarner Palace after an Austrian hotelier bought it in 2013.

tree: Immigration to South Africa, April 1975, from Zimbabwe
record: Family lore says 1948 — which the record will not allow
why: Her second and third children were born at Senj in December 1951 and April 1953, so the family was in Croatia at least five years after 1948. What 1948 is in this family is the birth of Ladislava at Crikvenica on 5 March. The crossing therefore happened after April 1953 and before about 1973, and this archive holds nothing at all from inside that span.

The Kosina grave at Senj reads KOSINA · KRIŽAN · ANKA, with Anka ✻?.X.1893 †6.IX.1953. The tree carried only the year. If so this is one of them. He is also the ancestor of the line that reached Port Pirie, so the date matters beyond him.

what: A child born after his death
why: Nineteen years — too wide for a posthumous child and too narrow to be obviously a different man. The Otočac Žubrinići repeat their given names relentlessly, and a record attached to the wrong Josephus would look exactly like this.

why: A hundred and eleven years. Not impossible, but in a tree with no death record cited for him it is far likelier that two men of one name have been merged — which the Otočac Žubrinići do constantly. Marked rather than corrected, because nothing here says which half is wrong.

tree: The Otočac baptism of Josephus, 16 March 1845, is attached to him — and gives the mother as Maria née Marković

A second Michael Miho Michaël Žubrinić, married to Maria Marković, has Theodorus 1841, Josephus 16 March 1845, Marta 1849 and Magdalena 1852. That is whose entry this is. The scan was filed under the wrong man, this archive read it, saw a wife née Marković where it expected née Orešković, and invented a second marriage to explain it. There was no second wife.

Senj baptisms str.107 no.65: Josip Papić, težak, i Tonka rodj. Prpić iz Krivog puta. Godparents Roko Stipanović, težak, and Mande Prpić. The place column reads simply Senj — no house number, where the village registers give Smokvica 114 and Krivi Put 136.

what: Baptism, and the grandfather confirmed by patronymic
tree: Born 5 November 1894, Novi Vinodolski, to Martin Kalanj and Marija Peričić
record: Born 5 November, baptised 11 November 1894 — and the father is entered as Martin Kalanj Josipov
why: Novi Vinodolski baptisms str.278 no.71: Ana, kći zakonita, of Martin Kalanj Josipov, žena mu Marija rodj. Peričić. The patronymic is the find: Josipov, son of Josip, matches the tree's Josip Josephus Joso Kalanj (b. 27 August 1826, Klenovica) independently of the tree. At page scale the mother's surname read as Crnić; at 3× it is Peričić, which is what the tree already said.

One of four consecutive siblings — Ana 1894, Franciska 1896, Zora 1898, Ivan 1900 — whose baptisms were all sitting unattached in the family's own photo library. Same parents, same parish, four scans.

what: A blank house-number column does not mean the household had no number
tree: This archive concluded on 13 September 2026 that “the house number is a village device and it does not reach the town”
record: Novi Vinodolski is a town, and its registers do give house numbers — just not to this family, and not on every page
why: The Senj finding stands as far as Senj goes. But the generalisation drawn from it — that the house number is a village device that does not reach the town — is refuted by four pages of Novi Vinodolski. On str.278 (1894) the column reads 110, 595, —, 313, 647, —, 476, —, —, —, 33, 631; on str.333 (1900) it reads —, 476, 684, 470, —, 223, 629, 103. Towns do record house numbers. On str.293 (1896) and str.314 (1898), by contrast, not one household is numbered at all. So the practice is per register and per priest. Two further things follow. A blank cell is not evidence that a household lacked a number — only that this entry does not record one. And on both pages where numbering happens, Martin Kalanj's household is among the blanks while his neighbours are numbered — which fits a family that came from Klenovica and may never have held a numbered house in Novi. His sister's 1864 baptism, back in the village, is entered Klenovica N° 22 without hesitation.

what: Her gravestone gives the wrong birth date
tree: Born 3 January 1864, Klenovica 22; died 28 May 1936, Crikvenica
record: The Crikvenica stone reads ✻ 19 IX 1863 — the baptismal register reads 3 January 1864
why: The grave at Crikvenica is inscribed ANA DE. FRANCESCHI ✻ 19 IX 1863 ✝ 28 V 1936. The death is exactly right. The birth is not. Her baptism survives: Anno Domini 1864, no. 2 — Anna, legitima, Josephus Kalanj et Rosalia nata Perković ejus uxor, Brinjensis parochiae ruricolae, at Klenovica N° 22, born 3 January 1864 and baptised three days later on 6 January. A register written within the week beats a stone cut after 1936, so the tree's date stands and the stone is the error. Worth saying plainly because the stone is the kind of source that feels conclusive and is not.

what: She is Martin Kalanj's sister, which explains the godparents
tree: Ana Kalanj and Martin Kalanj both children of Josip Kalanj and Rozalija Perković, Klenovica 22
record: Both baptisms name the same parents; and Ana's husband stands godfather to Martin's daughter
why: Ana's 1864 baptism gives her parents as Josephus Kalanj and Rosalia nata Perković at Klenovica 22 — the same couple the tree gives Martin (b. 8 November 1861, Klenovica 22). They are brother and sister. The confirmation arrives from an unexpected direction: at Zora Kalanj's baptism in 1898, Martin's daughter, the godparents are entered as Josip i Ana Defrancesco — that is Ana herself and her husband, the child's aunt and uncle. Four register pages, found loose in a photo library, turn out to document one household across two generations.
